key_insight: GBClaw links agentic AI-driven atomistic simulations with mechanistic analysis, revealing how defect hierarchies and metastable grain boundary structures influence sliding resistance in nickel.
engineering_relevance: Understanding how complex grain boundaries resist sliding could help guide microstructure design for polycrystalline materials.
method: Coordinate LLM-based specialist agents through an orchestrator, domain tools, simulation interfaces, and hierarchical memory.
Dynamically replan simulations and refine workflows to characterize boundary defects and deformation modes.
Compare sliding with and without secondary misfit dislocations, then investigate anomalies through researcher-guided calculations.
evidence_signal: Across 14 general asymmetric tilt grain boundaries in nickel, simulations revealed diverse deformation modes and substantial shear-strength differences associated with secondary misfit dislocations.
watch_item: Evidence is limited to 14 nickel boundaries, and the anomalous high-resistance mechanism required researcher-guided follow-up rather than fully autonomous discovery.
paper_title: GBClaw: An agentic AI framework for atomistic grain boundary research and mechanistic discovery
